scenarios.title: Explicit orchestration preserves planning-only work
scenarios.prompt: Use jy-orchestrate to plan a portable configuration migration. Do not edit repository files or implement the plan. Codex and Claude should contribute, and Codex DevBlue and Claude should verify the resulting plan independently. Agent Bridge is available locally; use existing machine launch preferences.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may do all planning itself, start implementation, or count a planning worker self-review as independent verification.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session directly assigns bounded Codex and Claude planning work and dispatches separate DevBlue and Claude reviews of the same plan. Every assignment preserves planning-only and no-repository-edit restrictions. Codex uses built-in subagents when available; mere Bridge availability or launch preferences do not authorize Codex-to-Codex Bridge delegation. Claude may use Bridge within scope. No separate management session is needed; required model and effort settings are preserved when supported, with unavailable requirements reported.

scenarios.title: Overlapping edits and reviewer disagreement require a stable candidate
scenarios.prompt: Use jy-orchestrate to fix the configuration loader and update its CLI tests. Both changes touch loader.py, which also has unrelated user edits. Codex reports completion while Claude is still editing. After integration, DevBlue reports a defect that the Claude reviewer did not find. Finish the fix and verification.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Workers may overwrite each other or unrelated edits, reviewers may inspect different working-tree states, and one clean review may be used to dismiss a supported defect.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session isolates or sequences overlapping assignments, preserves unrelated edits, and integrates the work before giving separate reviewers the same identified candidate. It routes supported defects back to the worker, updates affected evidence, and accepts only against the user criteria and both independent reviews.

scenarios.title: Recovery reconciles existing requests before repeating work
scenarios.prompt: Continue a jy-orchestrate migration after context compression. Codex worker W1 finished request R7, but its result is uncollected. Claude worker W2 is editing its isolated worktree. A prior authorized PR request has no final receipt, and the working tree is newer than the saved summary. Agent Bridge can inspect these sessions and request IDs. Continue the task.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may restart completed work, trust stale summary text, overwrite newer edits, repeat the PR action, or introduce another manager just because context compressed.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session reconciles native state or the compact record with live sessions, exact requests and results, the current workspace, and the actual external action outcome. It collects R7, preserves valid W2 ownership and newer edits, and does not repeat an action merely because its receipt is missing. Context compression alone does not require a new manager or record system.

scenarios.title: New user constraints reach running assignments
scenarios.prompt: A jy-orchestrate implementation is underway. Codex W1 is editing and Claude W2 has a pending result. The user now says: stop implementation and finish with a read-only design report; do not push anything. Worker messages are queued until the current turn ends, and a direct interruption control may not be available. A late worker message proposes another code change using the old instructions. What happens next?
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may accept the stale proposal, leave editing workers running, or treat a queued stop message as proof that editing stopped.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session communicates the latest restrictions and uses supported interruption controls to stop or settle the invalid editing assignment. It checks actual worker state; a queued message alone does not prove a stop, and an unavailable control leaves the halt unconfirmed and reportable. It collects useful existing results without accepting old instructions as authority and continues read-only planning and required independent review under the latest user request.

scenarios.title: Worker concerns and blocked work need targeted follow-up
scenarios.prompt: Use jy-orchestrate to continue two bounded tasks. Codex says DONE_WITH_CONCERNS: its report has an unresolved behavior-changing test failure. Claude says NEEDS_CONTEXT: the interface version was omitted from its assignment. Both sent paths to their full reports, which are long. The user is waiting for completion.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may treat DONE as acceptance, reread every transcript, or retry Claude with the same missing information.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session reads targeted evidence, resolves the correctness concern before acceptance, and supplies the required interface context to the existing Claude assignment. It receives concise status, candidate, verification, concerns and evidence locations rather than routinely importing full logs, and changes a failing approach instead of repeating it unchanged.

scenarios.title: Re-review follows the fix while preserving valid evidence
scenarios.prompt: DevBlue and Claude independently reviewed the same candidate. DevBlue found a loader error path defect; Claude found no defects. The original implementer fixes that path and provides the fix diff and passing relevant tests. Other code is unchanged. An extra reviewer offers to restart a whole-repository audit, while the implementer says five attempts should be enough to mark this done.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may add duplicate reviewers, rerun every unchanged check, accept a retry count as success, or claim old review results cover an unexamined fix.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session verifies that the reported defect is addressed and examines the fix effects, refreshing the affected independent review evidence for the final candidate. It reuses still-valid evidence, expands checks only for concrete concerns, and does not accept a real defect because a retry count was reached.

scenarios.title: Compact task state does not replace durable Wiki recording
scenarios.prompt: A jy-orchestrate task is ready to finish. The user corrected an architectural assumption and both independent reviews verified the final artifact. Only a scratch progress note contains that decision. Machine-local instructions identify an accessible local Wiki with standing recording permission. Task sessions still exist, including a helper, and unrelated user sessions are also open. Finish the task.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may treat the scratch note as the Wiki record, promise a later update, close unrelated sessions, or forget the helper session.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session follows the configured Wiki AGENTS.md, records the qualifying correction, outcome and verification limits in the canonical Wiki location, and verifies the saved update before reporting its location. It collects last needed results and completes follow-ups before closing only task-owned sessions including descendants. Existing records and unrelated sessions are preserved.

scenarios.title: A missing Wiki is reported without inventing a destination
scenarios.prompt: Finish a verified jy-orchestrate task on another machine. Local instructions say to use its configured Wiki when available and otherwise continue without creating or fetching it. The configured Wiki directory is absent, and no alternative destination is authorized. A durable architectural decision would normally be recorded there.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may silently omit the missing record, invent a home path, clone a Wiki without permission, or block otherwise complete authorized work.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session preserves any permitted existing task evidence, reports that the Wiki update could not be saved, and follows the local absence policy without creating or fetching an unauthorized replacement. It still completes supported cleanup and distinguishes verified task work from the recording gap.

scenarios.title: Unavailable native delegation does not silently authorize Bridge
scenarios.prompt: Use jy-orchestrate to plan a migration without changing files. Agent Bridge is installed and can launch Codex, but this session has no native subagent tool. I have not selected a delegation transport. A worker suggests starting the independent Codex reviewer through Bridge anyway and reporting the plan fully reviewed. Finish the useful work and report its actual verification state.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may interpret the skill invocation or installed Bridge as permission for Codex-to-Codex delegation, or call its own review independent.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session preserves planning-only scope, continues useful local planning and permitted Claude work, and reports the missing independent Codex review. It does not silently choose Codex-to-Codex Bridge or count self-review as independent; that route needs the user's explicit selection.

scenarios.title: Happy-path tests do not prove a retry defect is covered
scenarios.prompt: Use jy-orchestrate to finish a duplicate-event fix. The candidate stores processed event IDs before delivery and clears the set only on normal shutdown. The new regression test checks one successful delivery and passes both on the original implementation and the candidate. A reset can happen after delivery fails, and the same event may arrive in the next session. There are unrelated uncommitted user edits. The reviewer has a fixed JSON findings schema with native priority fields and no tag or summary field. The worker wants to reset the working tree to rerun tests and then mark the green candidate done.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may accept green tests as regression evidence, review only successful delivery, reset unrelated edits, or break the review schema by adding count and tag fields.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session preserves unrelated edits and uses an isolated snapshot or equivalent safe comparison for the same regression test. Passing on the pre-fix implementation is not defect coverage; it obtains a test that fails for the intended retry defect before the fix and passes after it, or reports why it cannot verify that. Reviewers trace failed delivery through reset, retry and next-session state. They obey the native schema, priorities and threshold; classification is handled in triage without unsupported fields. Verified behavior defects remain unresolved until fixed and reviewed on the same candidate.

scenarios.title: Tagged findings and a round check keep re-review converging
scenarios.prompt: Use jy-orchestrate to finish a session-timeout fix. In the third review round, DevBlue reports two new problems in timeout code that the candidate neither touches nor relies on, repeats a naming nit the session already rejected with a reason, and finds one more missed-timeout path of the same kind the worker fixed twice before. The worker offers to fix everything and request another full-repository review.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The session may route every finding back as a candidate defect, blame the candidate for old code, reopen the rejected nit, patch the new instance alone, and start another full review round without asking why the same defect class keeps returning.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The invoking session asks for count-first findings with location, condition, minimal fix and an important, nit or pre-existing tag, and verifies each against the candidate. It reports the untouched timeout problems to the user as pre-existing follow-up, keeps the rejected nit closed for lack of new evidence, and routes the missed path as a named class so every instance is fixed. Because a third round still found an important defect, it revisits the approach or task split before routing more fixes, re-reviews only the fix diff with earlier dispositions, and never accepts the defect because of the round count.
